title: LADDER: Language-Driven Slice Discovery and Error Rectification in Vision Classifiers

bias_targets.methodology: Projecting internal classifier activations into a vision-language representation space, retrieving descriptive text for misclassified versus correctly classified samples, and using an LLM to generate testable hypotheses about visual shortcuts (e.g., backgrounds in Waterbirds/MetaShift, chest tubes in X-rays, calcifications in mammograms). Performance is measured using Worst Group Accuracy (WGA) and Precision@10 on these discovered slices.

Evaluating model performance on the CelebA dataset, specifically measuring Worst Group Accuracy (WGA) to detect and mitigate the spurious correlation between the 'blond hair' classification and the female gender.

Extracting structured metadata from the RSNA-Mammo dataset (e.g., age, BIRADS score, implant presence), passing it to an LLM to generate bias hypotheses, and measuring the accuracy gap (e.g., a 19.5% drop in accuracy) for patients aged 70+ compared to younger demographics.
